subject: Control plane ↔ data plane interconnect - acceptance evidence & cutover checklist
messages:
From: Erin Walters <erin.walters@atlas-payments.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: netops@atlas-payments.com
Date: 2026-12-04T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Control plane/data plane interconnect - acceptance evidence request

Jonas,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Before we sign off on the private VPC cutover, our security and networking teams have asked for a concise acceptance packet that proves the control-plane <-> data-plane interconnect meets our compliance and routing constraints. Specifically we need:

- A one-page mapping of control plane endpoints, ports and expected egress ranges for each tenant slice.
- Proof that TLS is end-to-end (no user traffic terminating on the edge proxy) and cert rotation plan for the control channel.
- KMS integration details: whether keys stay in our KMS or Redwood envelopes with customer-managed keys.
- Expected SNAT behavior for outbound model calls (will connections source-NAT to the cluster egress IPs?)
- Audit/logging evidence: what traces/logs Redwood will provide for the control-plane handshake and token exchange.

We're trying to avoid surprises during our firewall cutover window next Wednesday (12/09). Can you send the packet and a short cutover checklist that our ops team can follow? Attachments (diagrams, snippets) are fine.

If helpful we can do a 30m sync today; Erin W. and our netops lead (cc'd) will be available after 2pm PT.

-Erin
Erin Walters
Sr. Network Engineer | Atlas Payments

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-04T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Control plane/data plane interconnect - acceptance evidence request

Erin — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a first-pass packet (ctrlplane-data-mapping-v1.pdf) and a cutover checklist spreadsheet (cutover-checklist.xlsx). High-level answers below; details are in the PDF and the checklist.

Summary answers:
- Control endpoints & ports: control-plane management endpoints will be reachable from tenant control hosts over TCP 443 (mutual TLS). The PDF maps each endpoint to a FQDN and expected port. We list the control plane CIDR(s) that must be permitted inbound from your control VLAN.
- TLS: mutual TLS is used for control-channel RPCs. No user request traffic terminates on the RL edge proxy — edge only handles SNI routing and forwards encrypted payloads to runtime nodes. Cert rotation: documented in section 3 of the PDF; rotation happens via our orchestration with a 7-day overlap window.
- KMS: we support an integration model where keys can remain in your KMS (recommended for regulated customers). We also offer envelope wrapping in Redwood for customers that need us to manage rotation. See appendix B.
- SNAT: by default outbound model invocations egress from the tenant runtime subnet and will SNAT to the tenant egress IPs you provision. We include a fallback ASN/NAT mapping if you prefer provider-side SNAT.
- Audit/logging: control-plane handshakes are logged to a per-tenant audit stream (syslog + encrypted S3 archive). We can provide a short sample log extract as evidence.

Action items we need from Atlas to finalize the packet:
1) Confirm control-plane consumer CIDR(s) and the egress IP(s) you will allow.
2) Confirm whether you want Redwood-managed envelope keys or your KMS.
3) Confirm acceptance criteria for the cutover sign-off (e.g., smoke tests, canary %).

Proposed timeline: if we get the CIDRs and KMS choice today, we'll provide a hardened acceptance packet by EOD and be ready for a 12/09 cutover.

Call: happy to take a 2pm PT sync.

Attachments: ctrlplane-data-mapping-v1.pdf, cutover-checklist.xlsx

--
Jonas Weber
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Adding a few technical clarifications and a minimal acceptance checklist items list (inline):

> Jonas: Cert rotation happens via our orchestration with a 7-day overlap window.

- Operational note: overlap window ensures no single-rotation causes token rejections during rolling restarts. We'll provide the rotation schedule and the cert fingerprint list in the final packet.

> SNAT: outbound model invocations egress from the tenant runtime subnet and will SNAT to the tenant egress IPs you provision.

- Proposed firewall rules (example):
  - Allow TCP/443 from tenant control CIDR(s) -> control-plane FQDNs
  - Allow ephemeral return ports for model streaming (we recommend pinning expected ephemeral range 32000-32767 to simplify ACLs)
  - Block outbound 25/445 unless explicitly required

Minimal acceptance checklist (for your ops):
1) Basic connectivity: ping/tcp 443 handshake to control FQDNs from your control-colocation hosts.
2) mTLS verification: exchange certificates and validate fingerprint via our provided tool (we'll provide a small script).
3) SNAT validation: from a runtime pod, curl an external echo service and verify source IP equals your tenant egress IP(s).
4) Observability: confirm you can read control-plane audit entries in the sample stream we deliver.

Telemetry/observability details: control-plane events include timestamp, tenant_id, action (auth, handshake, token_issue), node_id, and correlation_id. Retention and delivery options are configurable — default: 90 days in encrypted archive + 30 days hot index.

I attached a small snippet (egress-contract-snippets.txt) with example firewall statements you can drop into your edge ACLs.

Let us know if we should switch SNAT mode to provider-side for the cutover.

- Mina
Mina Haddad
Platform Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

Thanks Jonas / Mina — packet received and looks good on first pass. A few quick clarifications before we lock the cutover: 

- CIDRs: Confirmed; we'll open 10.240.16.0/22 from the control VLAN to your control endpoints.
- KMS: Atlas will keep keys in our cloud KMS (customer-managed). Please confirm the integration steps and whether we need to provision a service account.
- SNAT: We'll keep SNAT on customer side (preferred) — Mina's checklist step #3 is exactly what we will run.
- SOC2 evidence: our audit team asked whether the control-plane audit stream includes immutable event IDs and whether Redwood can provide a signed hash of the archive for the cutover snapshot. Can you include that in the evidence packet?

We'll plan the 12/09 cutover window but will only execute once we have the KMS integration playbook and the signed archive hash for the snapshot. If you can get those two items to us by EOD tomorrow, we'll be green to proceed. Otherwise we need to move the maintenance window.

I'll also join the 2pm PT sync today to walk through the checklist live.

-Erin
